failure_summary.description: Agents returned “No planning needed” despite new hotel, restaurant, or flight-budget criteria that needed filtering against cached results.
Agents imported the unavailable `tools` module instead of calling injected tool functions directly.
An agent treated a question about a just-proposed place as a request to display the old cache summary rather than applying the place as a criterion.
A missing hotel date prevented the agent from searching for requested restaurants whose required inputs were already available.
An attraction search placed a state abbreviation in `city` instead of the supported `state` parameter.
An attraction search result was not assigned and saved to the cache.

patch.reasoning: The main repeated failure is treating existing cached results as sufficient even when the user adds criteria. Make the cache check explicitly compare every current criterion and require filtering and saving unmet criteria. Clarify that missing inputs for one domain do not block independent, complete requested searches, and resolve contextual references to proposed places. Add the missing budget and geographic-field mappings. Direct tool calls and result caching are already explicit in the skill, so those rules are not duplicated.

edits.target: - Check mandatory inputs against the full conversation and relevant cached results before planning calls. Flight searches require a departure date; hotel searches require check-in and checkout dates. If any requested domain lacks required inputs, make exactly one `seek_information(...)` call listing only the missing required values across the requested domains. Do not make partial searches or other planning calls until the user provides them. Do not guess or invent values, and do not ask for optional preferences as if they were required. Once required inputs are available, continue with independent searches whose inputs are available.
edits.content: - Check mandatory inputs against the full conversation and relevant cached results separately for each requested domain. Flight searches require a departure date; hotel searches require check-in and checkout dates. If any requested domain lacks required inputs, make exactly one `seek_information(...)` call listing only the missing required values. Do not search or filter an incomplete domain. In the same turn, proceed with independent requested searches whose required inputs are complete; missing information for one domain does not block another. Do not guess or invent values, and do not ask for optional preferences as if they were required.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, search each leg separately, reverse the outbound route for the return, and use the return leg’s departure date. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route.
edits.content: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, search each leg separately, reverse the outbound route for the return, and use the return leg’s departure date. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route.

edits.target: - Match arguments to the tool schema’s expected type and cardinality. For a range-shaped field, encode one requested exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]` for one star rating). Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`).
edits.content: - Match arguments to the tool schema’s expected type, cardinality, and meaning. Map an explicitly stated spending amount to the corresponding `budget` parameter; when the tool’s budget is a maximum, use the stated amount even when phrased as “around” or “under.” For geographic fields, map a state name or abbreviation to `state`, not `city`; for a state-level attraction request, use `state` without requiring a city. For a range-shaped field, encode one requested exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]` for one star rating). Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`).

edits.target: - On each turn, consider the full conversation and cached result summaries. Reuse cached results only when their domain and subject match the request. If the user adds criteria, retrieve the closest compatible result, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result. Do not filter unrelated results; search for a requested entity or category that the cached results do not cover. Avoid retrieving unrelated results or repeating constraints in filters that were already applied. Save each newly generated search or transformation result under a unique cache key. Use “No planning needed” only when cached results already satisfy every current request.
edits.content: - On each turn, compare every current request and criterion from the full conversation with compatible cached result summaries. Reuse results only when their domain and subject match. A result’s existence, item count, or broad coverage does not show that it satisfies a criterion unless the summary supports that criterion. When a user adds a criterion not already satisfied by a compatible cached result, retrieve the closest result, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result under a unique cache key. Apply new criteria to every affected result set, including each affected flight leg. Do not filter unrelated results; search for a requested entity or category the cache does not cover. Avoid repeating constraints already applied. Use “No planning needed” only when compatible cached results explicitly satisfy every current request and criterion and no further operation is needed.
